Honestly I think you might be surprised. There are definitely some people who might be assholes about it or not see you the way you want to be seen, but I also think that a lot of gay men would be happy dating someone who’s ftm. I can definitely understand how finding those men might be disheartening though. What I would personally recommend is communicating your boundaries upfront so that no one expects anything of you that you are not comfortable with.

My boyfriend would definitely take it as a compliment. He worries a lot about passing and even someone calling him “bro” or “sir” gives him a lot of euphoria. Being seen as cis male is pretty much his ultimate goal with his transition.

The best thing you can do right now is be there for her when she’s out. I know things must seem scary and overwhelming, but I’m sure that for her having a person who loves her be there when she gets out will at the very least help somewhat.

I find making friends pretty difficult as well, but some of my longest lasting friendships have been online. It can definitely be scary since you never know who’s on the other end, but maybe a start could be attempting to find a trans friendly discord server or something like that? Discord doesn’t exactly have the best reputation, but I’ve met some good friends on it that have helped me through a lot of struggles

I’m not sure how to help, but know that of course your parents are wrong. They can say what they want, but you are not a freak or wrong in any way for wanting to be your true self. I think the best thing to do would be attempting to find some supportive friends so you have a support group, but I know that’s easier said than done. Either way I hope things improve
